clue.text: A garland (American, of course) turning us right up before it becomes something to enjoy

indicators.note: before places the preceding pieces ahead of the final word in the answer

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian flower garland, and Hawaii is an American state
of course means sure, certainly

indicators.note: turning signals that the words us, right and up are read backwards as one run

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzling description of an American flower garland being turned about before becoming a source of pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses US R UP to give PURSU, which is followed by IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastime or hobby is an activity taken up for enjoyment in spare time.

clue.text: Smiley's pleader a suspect? I'm not at liberty to say

definitions.text: I'm not at liberty to say

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, not genuine, so the preceding letters are not in their true order

explanation.surface: Is the advocate for a spymaster called Smiley a suspicious character? Sorry, that is confidential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges SMILEYSPLEADERA. Smiley is the spymaster in John le Carré's novels, which adds to the secretive surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiomatic way of refusing to reveal a secret, just like declaring one cannot say.

clue.text: Language bound to cause difficulty in speaking

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for the adjective: having this difficulty is the state described

parts.note: a tongue is a language, as in mother tongue
bound means tied up

explanation.surface: A language that is certain to make speech hard for learners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cause' is link wording; the definition describes the condition of a person who cannot get words out.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone too shy or flustered to speak freely is described with this adjective.

clue.text: A principle to be discerned in group receptions

indicators.note: the answer can be discerned, seen, lying inside the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A guiding rule that can be noticed at gatherings of many people.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across grouP RECEPTions.
explanation.definitionFit: A precept is a rule or guiding standard of conduct, the same as a principle.

clue.text: One will be good enough for Liberal's image

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to do means to suffice, as in 'that will do'
L is the abbreviation for Liberal in politics

explanation.surface: Somebody satisfied with the public picture of a Liberal politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' and ''s' are link words joining the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a graven image, a figure worshipped as a god.

clue.text: Go to dinner, say, clutching book — one's first experience of split up

parts.note: to go is to depart, leave

indicators.note: clutching means holding inside, so the meal surrounds the book

parts.note: dinner is an example of a meal
NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible
one's gives I (one) plus 'S, written IS

indicators.note: first picks just the opening letter of the word that follows it

explanation.surface: Someone heading off to dinner with a book in hand, describing a first encounter with being divided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clutching' sets the book inside the meal to make the 'mental' stretch; 'dinner, say' signals an example, not dinner itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To departmentalise is to divide an organisation into separate sections, to split it up.

clue.text: Little squirt preventing us getting a bite

definitions.text: Little squirt preventing us getting a bite

parts.words: Little squirt preventing us getting a bite
parts.note: a little squirt sounds like a cheeky small person, but here it is a spray that stops bugs biting us

explanation.definitionFit: A spray or lotion that deters mosquitoes and midges keeps them from biting.

clue.text: An integral part of the house

definitions.text: An integral part of the house

parts.words: An integral part of the house
parts.note: house reads as a building, but here it is the audience in a theatre, of which each ticket-holder is a member

explanation.definitionFit: A theatregoer is one member of the audience, which theatre people call the house.

clue.text: Older woman hanging over girl's back

parts.note: a debt hanging over you is outstanding, due

indicators.note: back signals that the girl's name is read backwards

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A mature lady leaning over a young woman's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hanging over' suggests leaning, but here it means a debt still outstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman acting as chaperone to girls in Spanish families.

clue.text: Old number Elvis called "Old Sea Dog"

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral for six, an old way of writing a number
Elvis Presley was called the King of rock and roll

explanation.surface: A classic song which Elvis titled 'Old Sea Dog'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old number' suggests a vintage song, but it is the Roman numeral VI.
explanation.definitionFit: A Viking was a Norse seafarer of old, a seasoned sailor and raider.

clue.text: Brought together, indifferent about being delayed

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the second

parts.note: a cold manner is an indifferent one
delayed means late

explanation.surface: Gathered together, unconcerned about running behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link word; 'about' is the container signal, not 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: To collate pages is to gather them together in order.

clue.text: Back at university someone's emptied the kitty

indicators.note: back signals the words at university are turned round

parts.note: being up means being in residence at university

indicators.note: emptied means removing the inside, leaving only the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Back at college, somebody has spent all the shared fund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses UP to PU; 'emptied' leaves the first and last letters S and S of someone's.
explanation.definitionFit: Puss and kitty are both pet names for a cat.

clue.text: Deprive of three claws and despatch quickly without thanks

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first word goes round the second

parts.note: to expedite is to speed up or despatch quickly
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: Instructions to declaw an animal and hurry it off without a word of gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. Expeditating was the old English forest-law practice of cutting claws from dogs' forefeet to stop them chasing deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Expeditation meant cutting off the three front claws of a dog's forefoot under English forest law.

clue.text: An asinine performance?

parts.note: asinine usually means foolish, but literally it means like an ass, so this is literally work done by an ass

explanation.definitionFit: Drudgery or tedious hard labour is called this after the beast of burden.

clue.text: Letter lost, allowed to fall on the ground

indicators.note: lost signals that part of the word letter goes missing

parts.note: allowed means let
rain is to fall from the sky

explanation.surface: A letter goes missing, then is dropped on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like a written note, but it is the word itself, with 'allowed' naming the part that is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is a stretch of land considered for its physical features, the ground.

clue.text: Emphatically accepting choice when provided with a list of subjects

definitions.text: provided with a list of subjects

indicators.note: accepting means taking inside, so the first word holds the second

parts.note: indeed is used emphatically, as in 'very good indeed'
X marks a choice on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: Insisting firmly on taking a selection once furnished with a catalogue of topics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts X inside INDEED; 'when' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A book given an alphabetical list of topics at the back has been indexed.

clue.text: Pouring out for us exclusively

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the preceding word are disordered, put out of place

explanation.surface: Serving drinks only for ourselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges POURING.
explanation.definitionFit: A clique or select set reserved for members only, keeping outsiders away.

clue.text: Settling down with advance team, getting directions to capture castle, initially

parts.note: a sub is an advance on wages
a side is a team

indicators.note: to capture means to hold inside, so the directions surround a letter

parts.note: N and E are the compass directions north and east

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: An army settles in with a forward unit, given orders to take a fortress first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to capture' puts C (from castle, picked by 'initially') inside NE to give NCE; 'with' and 'getting' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Subsidence is the gradual sinking or settling of ground or a building.

clue.text: Swarm seen in retrospect as seemly

indicators.note: looking back in retrospect signals reading the word backwards

parts.note: meet is an old word for fitting or seemly

explanation.surface: A crowd looks back on events as having been proper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in retrospect' reverses MEET; 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To teem is to be crowded or swarming with life.

clue.text: Pear lies rotten by fruit tree

indicators.note: rotten fruit is spoilt, so the letters before it are spoilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A pear lies decaying beside the tree it fell from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotten' rearranges PEARLIES; 'by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An espalier is a fruit tree trained flat against a wall or trellis.

clue.text: Ten volunteers is not much

parts.note: IO resembles the figure 10, one and zero
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Ten volunteers make only a small force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word. The Territorial Army (TA) is the British Army's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the smallest Greek letter, used to mean a tiny amount.

clue.text: Ignoring the alternatives, whirls Dolly with exuberance

indicators.note: skipping every other letter of the following words, keeping only the alternate ones that remain

explanation.surface: Someone spinning Dolly round without a thought for other choices.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep W, I, L from whirls and D, L, Y from Dolly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something wildly means doing it in an unrestrained, exuberant manner.

clue.text: Steer straight

definitions.meaning: a verb: to guide or manage a course
an adjective: going in a straight line without deviation

explanation.definitionFit: To direct is to steer; a direct route is a straight one.

clue.text: First member of union forcing open rebellion

indicators.note: picks out the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: prising means forcing open with a lever

explanation.surface: A trade union leader wrenching open a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: U from union goes before PRISING.
explanation.definitionFit: An uprising is a popular revolt against authority.
